name: Empirical Bayes normal means (ebnm)
title: How much to trust each program's own number
what: Learn from the data how programs vary, then shrink each noisy number by the right amount. No tuning.
pick_line: An “is this move real?” flag for every program in each budget cycle.
data: SYNTHETIC mock budgets (Corning_mock, MS_mock), not any firm's budget
one: It finds 6–7× more real moves than BH, with almost no wrong signs.

right.sub: called, all with the right sign

findings.h: It finds 6–7× more real moves, with almost no wrong signs.
findings.t: Calls of “this program really changed”: 91 vs 14 (Corning mock) and 200 vs 28 (MS mock). Wrong sign: 0% and 1.5%.

findings.h: Pooling cuts each program's level error by about a quarter.
findings.t: Log RMSE 0.146 → 0.108 (Corning mock) and 0.138 → 0.109 (MS mock). Programs alone in their group lose a little (0.110 → 0.120).

chart.title: Error in 2025 level (log RMSE, lower is better)

findings.h: Honest: shrinkage adds nothing to the text-vs-numbers check.
findings.t: Comparing with peers does the work. On the MS mock: AUC 0.777 with ebnm, 0.775 with a plain z-score.

chart.title: Finding “says grow, actually shrinking” (MS mock AUC)

findings.h: Build 2026-11-23: our own port matches ebnm; the flag test misses one calibration bar.
findings.t: With the same scale grid the port matches ebnm to 1.5e-12 in log-likelihood. On mocks regenerated with a new seed (pre-registered): 1.9% / 1.8% wrong signs among flags, 107 vs 0 and 163 vs 42 BH calls, 0% false flags with no true effects, but the MS lfsr 0.2–0.5 bin is off by 5.4 points (bar ±5).

findings.h: Build 2026-11-23: Rust is faster, but not 5× faster.
findings.t: The same solver in NumPy and Rust both match ebnm to 8e-12. One fit at 998 programs: 3.17 ms (NumPy) vs 1.36 ms (Rust) vs 13 ms (R). The keep-Rust rule needs 5×; we got 2.3×, and NumPy alone misses the 3 ms bar by 0.17 ms.

chart.title: One ash fit, 998 programs, ms (lower is better)
